spatial_entity.notes: Historical island production context. Stone Town point is a modern navigation proxy on Unguja, not the plantation distribution or polity boundary.

claim.spatial_precision: Unguja and Pemba island production system; plantation distribution not encoded as a polygon
claim.summary: Specialist economic history identifies slave-based production of cloves, coconuts and sugar on Unguja and Pemba and links that production system to the slave trade during the nineteenth-century Zanzibar commercial economy. The 1859–1870/71 interval is used as a bounded source-data window, not as a universal prevalence surface.
claim.notes: Do not convert export-value shares into prevalence of slavery, and do not infer that every locality or resident on the islands participated in the system.

territorial_practice.notes: Positive island production-system classification; trade/network finance remains a separate analytical dimension. No P-level.

source.title: Slaves, Spices and Ivory in Zanzibar: Integration of an East African Commercial Empire into the World Economy, 1770–1873
source.geographic_scope: Zanzibar, Unguja and Pemba with mainland commercial connections
source.independence_notes: Single specialist synthesis; quantitative tables and narrative are one evidentiary family.
source.reliability_limitations: Commercial/export evidence describes an island production system and wider commercial empire; it is not a locality-level prevalence map.

evidence.evidence_role: specialist synthesis of slave-based island production
evidence.locator: Chapter 'The Structure of the Commercial Empire', pp. 116–154; discussion of slave-based production on Unguja and Pemba and 1859–1870/71 export data.
